editor_note: "Classical feedforward" has two different translations. The page title [1] uses "Anticipation classique", while [0], [6] and [15] use "rétroaction classique", which strictly means feedback. The term should be the same everywhere, and "commande par anticipation" or "anticipation classique" would be more accurate. In [29], "un seul bloc est exécuté à la fois" means "one block at a time" rather than "only one block is ever executed", which weakens the no-fallthrough point. There are also smaller wording issues: "élever" for lifting a value in [43], and "calendrier du circuit" for circuit schedule in [52], where "ordonnancement" is the usual term.

editor_note: The dated qualifier "As of July 2025" is translated as "Depuis juillet 2025" in notes 4, 6 and 7. It does have calques and a few loose renderings. "Grant writing" is calqued throughout as "rédaction de subventions" / "rédiger des subventions" where French would say "rédaction de demandes de subvention". "Benchmarking" is rendered as "étalonnage" in [34], [48], [78] and [80], which a quantum reader will take to mean qubit calibration. The DOE "Basic Energy Sciences quantum calls" cell becomes "Appels à la science fondamentale sur l'énergie quantique", which garbles the office name into a made-up topic. "Quantum-safe cybersecurity" becomes the muddled "cybersécurité quantique sécurisée". Smaller slips: "Correspondre aux initiatives" (should be "S'aligner sur"), "Ce qui suit sont", and English-order dates such as "fév. 19, 2026".

examples.source: Basic Energy Sciences quantum calls
examples.translation: Appels à la science fondamentale sur l'énergie quantique
examples.suggested: Appels « quantique » du programme Basic Energy Sciences (BES)
examples.why: The translation turns a DOE office name into an invented topic, 'quantum energy'.

examples.source: reliable deliverables include benchmarking, comparisons of methods
examples.translation: des livrables fiables comme les étalonnages, les comparaisons de méthodes
examples.suggested: des livrables fiables comme le benchmarking (évaluation comparative des performances), les comparaisons de méthodes
examples.why: In a QC context 'étalonnage' means calibration, a different activity. The same rendering recurs in [48], [78] and [80].

examples.source: quantum-safe cybersecurity skills for migration to post-quantum cryptography
examples.translation: les compétences en cybersécurité quantique sécurisée
examples.suggested: les compétences en cybersécurité résistante au quantique
examples.why: 'Quantum-safe' means resistant to quantum attacks. 'Quantique sécurisée' is garbled.

examples.source: you likely know how to write grants very well ... map them into the space of quantum computing
examples.translation: tu sais probablement très bien comment rédiger des subventions ... les cartographier dans l'espace de l'informatique quantique
examples.suggested: tu sais sans doute très bien rédiger des demandes de subvention ... les transposer au domaine de l'informatique quantique
examples.why: Calque of 'write grants' and 'map into the space'. The same calque runs through the whole page.

examples.source: Match agency initiatives (both strategic goals and timelines).
examples.translation: Correspondre aux initiatives des agences
examples.suggested: S'aligner sur les initiatives des agences (objectifs stratégiques comme calendriers).
examples.why: This use of 'correspondre' is ungrammatical as an imperative-infinitive instruction.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing would mislead a learner, but several calques need fixing. "Grant writing" is rendered as "rédaction de subventions" in [5] and [11], which literally means writing the grants themselves; it should be "rédaction de demandes de subvention". [20] repeats "à l'échelle" awkwardly ("adoption à l'échelle entreprise à l'échelle mondiale"), and [29] has a calque that is not grammatical ("créent des voies d'accès pour les talents diversifiés à contribuer"). "Academic institutions" appears as "Établissements d'enseignement" in [17]/[21] and as "établissement académique" in [25], and in [27] "responsibly" has shifted to "raisonnablement".

examples.source: Grant writing - mapping best practices in general for grant writing
examples.translation: Rédaction de subventions - application des meilleures pratiques générales de rédaction de subventions
examples.suggested: Rédaction de demandes de subvention - application des bonnes pratiques générales de rédaction de demandes de subvention
examples.why: In French you write a grant application, not a grant. 'Rédaction de subventions' is a literal calque; the same problem appears in [5].

examples.source: by enabling enterprise-grade adoption at a global scale
examples.translation: en permettant une adoption à l'échelle entreprise à l'échelle mondiale
examples.suggested: en permettant une adoption de niveau entreprise à l'échelle mondiale
examples.why: 'À l'échelle' appears twice in a row, and 'à l'échelle entreprise' is a stiff calque of 'enterprise-grade'.

examples.source: create on-ramps for diverse talent to contribute
examples.translation: créent des voies d'accès pour les talents diversifiés à contribuer
examples.suggested: offrent à des talents variés des voies d'accès pour contribuer
examples.why: This copies the English 'for X to do Y' structure, which French does not allow; the sentence is not grammatical as written.

examples.source: data that cannot legally or responsibly be shared over the Internet
examples.translation: des données qui ne peuvent légalement ou raisonnablement pas être partagées
examples.suggested: des données qui ne peuvent pas, légalement ou de manière responsable, être partagées
examples.why: 'Raisonnablement' (reasonably) weakens the ethical sense of 'responsibly', and the placement of the negation is awkward.

examples.source: (academic institution, large enterprise, and so on)
examples.translation: (établissement académique, grande entreprise, etc.)
examples.suggested: (établissement d'enseignement, grande entreprise, etc.)
examples.why: [17] and [21] call the same category 'Établissements d'enseignement', so this line should match.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the Eastin-Knill statement, the distiller outcome conditions and Steane/Knill error correction, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix several calques and two grammar slips. The first is "overhead" rendered as "frais généraux" (an accounting term) instead of "surcoût", together with "selon ces lignes". The others are "il peut être qu'une porte … peut être" and "Bien que … pourrait" (both need the subjunctive), "soi-disant *état chat*" (pejorative in French), "augmentation dramatique" and "susceptible aux erreurs".

examples.source: the overhead for using magic states to implement gates fault-tolerantly along these lines would be extremely high
examples.translation: les frais généraux liés à l'utilisation d'états magiques … selon ces lignes seraient extrêmement élevés
examples.suggested: le surcoût lié à l'utilisation d'états magiques … de cette manière serait extrêmement élevé
examples.why: 'Frais généraux' is accounting vocabulary. In computing the usual word for overhead is 'surcoût'. 'Selon ces lignes' is a literal calque of 'along these lines'.

examples.source: it may be that a particular gate can be implemented transversally with one code but not the other
examples.translation: il peut être qu'une porte particulière peut être implémentée transversalement
examples.suggested: il se peut qu'une porte donnée puisse être implémentée transversalement
examples.why: Calqued syntax, and the subjunctive is missing after 'il se peut que'.

examples.source: Although any of these gates could fail and introduce an error
examples.translation: Bien que l'une quelconque de ces portes pourrait défaillir
examples.suggested: Bien que n'importe laquelle de ces portes puisse défaillir
examples.why: 'Bien que' requires the subjunctive, and 'l'une quelconque' reads stiffly.

examples.source: using a so-called *cat state,*
examples.translation: à l'aide d'un soi-disant *état chat*
examples.suggested: à l'aide d'un état dit *état chat*
examples.why: In French 'soi-disant' implies doubt or disparagement, while the English 'so-called' is neutral terminology.

examples.source: which can cause the number of errors to increase dramatically
examples.translation: ce qui peut entraîner une augmentation dramatique du nombre d'erreurs
examples.suggested: ce qui peut faire augmenter considérablement le nombre d'erreurs
examples.why: Anglicism: 'dramatique' means tragic in French, not large or sudden.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the CSS compatibility condition in [79], the parity-check counting in [27] and [67], and the Steane code-space example in [97]. Nothing here would mislead a learner. There are a few native-editor fixes. "Collapses" in [65] became the anglicism "se collapse", and "effectively" was dropped. "Oblivious to both" in [62] became "complètement indépendants", which is less precise than "insensibles". The term "générateurs $Z$ stabilisateurs" is used consistently, but its word order is unusual; "générateurs stabilisateurs de type $Z$" is the more natural form. Finally, "inner product" is calqued as "produit intérieur" in [26].

examples.source: an arbitrary error on this number of qubits effectively collapses probabilistically into some combination of X errors, Z errors, or both
examples.translation: une erreur arbitraire sur ce nombre de qubits se collapse probabilistiquement en une combinaison d'erreurs X, d'erreurs Z, ou des deux
examples.suggested: une erreur arbitraire sur ce nombre de qubits se réduit en pratique, de façon probabiliste, à une combinaison d'erreurs X, d'erreurs Z, ou des deux
examples.why: 'se collapser' is an anglicism, and the qualifier 'effectively' was dropped.

examples.source: so they're completely oblivious to both
examples.translation: donc ils en sont complètement indépendants
examples.suggested: donc ils y sont complètement insensibles
examples.why: 'Oblivious' means the generators do not detect these operations. 'Indépendants' is vaguer and could be confused with the statistical independence of X and Z correction mentioned in the same paragraph.

examples.source: Z stabilizer generators
examples.translation: générateurs $Z$ stabilisateurs
examples.suggested: générateurs stabilisateurs de type $Z$
examples.why: The term is used consistently but the word order sounds unnatural. French QEC texts usually say 'générateurs (stabilisateurs) de type Z'. This is minor and the concept is still clear.

examples.source: the binary dot product is not an inner product in a formal sense
examples.translation: le produit scalaire binaire n'est pas un produit intérieur au sens formel
examples.suggested: le produit scalaire binaire n'est pas un produit scalaire au sens formel (forme bilinéaire définie positive)
examples.why: 'Produit intérieur' is a calque. Standard French uses 'produit scalaire', so a short gloss is needed to keep the distinction.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The surface, rotated, color and gross code passages keep every quantity and condition: one qubit instead of two, distance 5, [[19,1,5]], weight 6, 12 qubits versus two. A native editor would still fix a few slips. In [21], "aucune deux faces de la même couleur ne partagent" is ungrammatical. [2] has the anglicism "exemples prominents" and the calque "gratter un peu la surface". [18] uses the anglicism "ce pattern de base" where "schéma" or "motif" is the usual word.

examples.source: in such a way that no two faces of the same color share an edge
examples.translation: de sorte qu'aucune deux faces de la même couleur ne partagent une arête
examples.suggested: de sorte que deux faces de même couleur ne partagent jamais d'arête
examples.why: 'aucune deux faces' is ungrammatical in French. It is a word-for-word calque of 'no two faces'.

examples.source: we will scratch the surface just a bit to briefly examine a couple of prominent examples
examples.translation: nous allons gratter un peu la surface pour examiner brièvement quelques exemples prominents
examples.suggested: nous allons simplement effleurer le sujet en examinant brièvement quelques exemples marquants
examples.why: 'prominents' is an anglicism; 'proéminent' means physically protruding in French. 'Gratter la surface' is a calque of the English idiom.

examples.source: that generalize this basic pattern
examples.translation: qui généralisent ce pattern de base
examples.suggested: qui généralisent ce schéma de base
examples.why: 'Pattern' is an unnecessary English loanword here. 'Schéma' or 'motif' is the natural French word.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. I found no semantic drift in the harder passages: the two-outcome, rank-2^{n-1} argument in [49]–[50], the Bell-state non-collapse in [55] and the single-control-qubit reasoning in [63] are all faithful. Terminology is correct and consistent (ensemble engendré, groupe de Pauli, poids, mesure projective, retournement de bit/phase, estimation de phase). A native editor would still fix a few English calques: "mesure projective uniquement définie" in [35] (it can read as "only defined"), "il est conventionnel" in [8], "Il est typique que" in [19] and "multipliant ces matrices ensemble" in [22].

examples.source: a certain uniquely defined projective measurement
examples.translation: une certaine mesure projective uniquement définie
examples.suggested: une mesure projective bien déterminée, définie de manière unique
examples.why: This copies the English word order. In French, "uniquement définie" can be read as "only defined" rather than "uniquely defined".

examples.source: it is conventional to instead use the capital letters
examples.translation: il est conventionnel d'utiliser plutôt les lettres majuscules
examples.suggested: il est d'usage d'utiliser plutôt les lettres majuscules
examples.why: "Il est conventionnel" is a calque. "Il est d'usage" is the idiomatic phrase.

examples.source: It's typical that quantum error correcting codes are designed so that...
examples.translation: Il est typique que les codes correcteurs d'erreurs quantiques soient conçus...
examples.suggested: En général, les codes correcteurs d'erreurs quantiques sont conçus...
examples.why: "Il est typique que" is translationese. A French technical writer would write "En général" or "Typiquement".

examples.source: by multiplying these matrices together
examples.translation: en multipliant ces matrices ensemble
examples.suggested: en multipliant ces matrices entre elles
examples.why: "Multiplier ... ensemble" is a calque of "multiply together". The idiomatic French is "entre elles".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The query-model cost comparison, the "Search" procedure's f(x)=1 / f(x)=0 branches and the t = O(√N) claim with its "si elle existe" caveat all match the English, and the terms are consistent (porte de requête de phase, rétroaction de phase, qubit d'espace de travail). A few English calques remain that a native editor would smooth. "n'a aucune dépendance sur la fonction f" should be "ne dépend pas de f". "Mesurer … par rapport aux mesures en base standard" is awkward. "avec haute probabilité" should be "avec une forte probabilité". "suivie de la description" in [3] has a dangling agreement.

examples.source: the operation $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ has no dependence on the function $f$
examples.translation: l'opération $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ n'a aucune dépendance sur la fonction $f$
examples.suggested: l'opération $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ ne dépend pas de la fonction $f$
examples.why: Literal calque of 'has no dependence on'; not idiomatic French.

examples.source: Measure the qubits of $\mathsf{Q}$ with respect to standard basis measurements
examples.translation: Mesurer les qubits de $\mathsf{Q}$ par rapport aux mesures en base standard
examples.suggested: Mesurer les qubits de $\mathsf{Q}$ dans la base standard
examples.why: 'par rapport aux mesures' is a word-for-word rendering; French says 'mesurer dans la base standard'.

examples.source: with high probability
examples.translation: avec haute probabilité
examples.suggested: avec une forte probabilité
examples.why: 'avec haute probabilité' is an anglicism; the usual phrasing is 'avec une forte (grande) probabilité'.

examples.source: We'll begin by discussing phase query gates and how to build them, followed by the description of Grover's algorithm itself.
examples.translation: Nous commencerons par discuter des *portes de requête de phase* et de la façon de les construire, suivie de la description de l'algorithme de Grover lui-même.
examples.suggested: Nous commencerons par présenter les *portes de requête de phase* et la façon de les construire, puis nous décrirons l'algorithme de Grover lui-même.
examples.why: 'suivie de' has no correct antecedent to agree with; a calque of the English participle.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The probability bounds (1 - 2^{-m}, 1 - N^{-m}, 1 - s/N), the overshoot toward -|A_0⟩ when s=4, the 5/4-versus-doubling growth of T and the trivial cases all match the English. The problems are English calques a native editor would rewrite: "En résolvant pour t", "Il peut cependant être prouvé", "Comme exemple motivant", "avec une haute probabilité", and "légèrement particulière … plus la borne inférieure est mauvaise". Terminology is correct and consistent: requête, itérations, sous-espace engendré, borne inférieure, résultat de mesure.

examples.source: Solving for $t$ yields
examples.translation: En résolvant pour $t,$ on obtient
examples.suggested: En résolvant en $t$, on obtient
examples.why: 'Résoudre pour' is a calque of 'solve for'. French says 'résoudre en t' or 'en isolant t'.

examples.source: It can, however, be proved in general that
examples.translation: Il peut cependant être prouvé en général que
examples.suggested: On peut cependant montrer, en général, que
examples.why: The English passive construction is kept word for word. French mathematical prose uses 'on peut montrer'. The same calque appears in [54].

examples.source: leads to success with high probability
examples.translation: conduit à un succès avec une haute probabilité
examples.suggested: permet de réussir avec une forte probabilité
examples.why: The idiomatic collocation is 'forte probabilité', not 'haute probabilité'.

examples.source: is slightly peculiar in that more solutions implies a worse lower bound
examples.translation: est légèrement particulière en ce sens que plus il y a de solutions, plus la borne inférieure est mauvaise
examples.suggested: est quelque peu curieuse : plus il y a de solutions, plus la borne inférieure est faible
examples.why: 'Légèrement particulière' calques 'slightly peculiar', and 'mauvaise' is a stiff way to describe a bound. 'Curieuse' and 'faible' are the natural choices.

examples.source: As a motivating example
examples.translation: Comme exemple motivant
examples.suggested: Pour illustrer, prenons un exemple
examples.why: 'Exemple motivant' is a literal calque that sounds unnatural in French teaching prose.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and does not mislead. "matrices densité", "vecteurs d'état quantique", "applications linéaires" and "valeurs propres" are correct and used consistently, and the tu register holds. A native editor would still change three things. In [11], "est un aspect qui les rend d'une importance cruciale" shifts the emphasis: the English says the linear-map link is a critically important aspect of density matrices, not that it makes them crucially important. Also in [11], "l'aléatoire" as a bare noun is stiff. In the tooltip in [9], "entrées hors diagonale" is an anglicism; French math writing uses "coefficients" or "éléments hors diagonale".

examples.source: is a critically important aspect of them
examples.translation: est un aspect qui les rend d'une importance cruciale
examples.suggested: en constitue un aspect d'une importance cruciale
examples.why: The French says the aspect makes density matrices crucially important. The English says the aspect itself is critically important. The shift is small and does not mislead.

examples.source: describe the randomness or uncertainty inherent to the states
examples.translation: décrivent l'aléatoire ou l'incertitude inhérente aux états
examples.suggested: décrivent le caractère aléatoire ou l'incertitude inhérents aux états
examples.why: 'l'aléatoire' as a bare noun reads stiffly in technical French. 'le caractère aléatoire' is the usual phrasing.

examples.source: all of its off-diagonal entries are zero
examples.translation: toutes ses entrées hors diagonale sont nulles
examples.suggested: tous ses coefficients hors diagonale sont nuls
examples.why: 'entrées' calques the English 'entries'. French linear algebra says 'coefficients' or 'éléments' of a matrix.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: no inverted conditions, dropped caveats or invented claims, and the tu register holds ("Considère la simulation…"). There is one terminology slip. "inner product" is rendered as "produit intérieur" in [24], but the usual French term is "produit scalaire". Several calques would stand out to a native editor. "conditionné sur" appears in [40], [55], [58], [62] and [68], where French would say "conditionnellement à". [11] has "il est tracé" and ends on a stiff trailing "cependant". [41] has "infiniment nombreuses", and [37] uses "la correction de la simulation" where "la validité" reads more naturally.

examples.source: We can compute the inner product between any two of them as follows.
examples.translation: Nous pouvons calculer le produit intérieur entre deux quelconques d'entre eux comme suit.
examples.suggested: Nous pouvons calculer le produit scalaire de deux quelconques d'entre eux comme suit.
examples.why: 'Produit intérieur' is a calque. French linear algebra uses 'produit scalaire'.

examples.source: ...and can imagine that it is traced out. We'll be interested in the state of X after U is performed later in the lesson, though.
examples.translation: ...et nous pouvons imaginer qu'il est tracé. Nous nous intéresserons à l'état de X après que U est effectuée plus tard dans la leçon, cependant.
examples.suggested: ...et on peut imaginer qu'on en prend la trace partielle. Plus loin dans la leçon, en revanche, nous nous intéresserons à l'état de X après l'application de U.
examples.why: 'Il est tracé' is jargon calqued from English. The trailing 'cependant' copies English word order, and the misplaced 'plus tard' is ambiguous.

examples.source: the state of X conditioned on each possible measurement outcome
examples.translation: l'état de X conditionné sur chaque résultat de mesure possible
examples.suggested: l'état de X conditionnellement à chaque résultat de mesure possible
examples.why: 'Conditionné sur' calques 'conditioned on' and recurs in [40], [58], [62] and [68]. French probability writing uses 'conditionnellement à'.

examples.source: there will be multiple (in fact infinitely many) non-destructive measurements
examples.translation: il existera plusieurs (en fait infiniment nombreuses) mesures non destructives
examples.suggested: il existe plusieurs (en fait une infinité de) mesures non destructives
examples.why: 'Infiniment nombreuses' is awkward. 'Une infinité de' is the idiomatic phrasing.

examples.source: establishing the correctness of the simulation
examples.translation: établissant la correction de la simulation
examples.suggested: ce qui établit la validité de la simulation
examples.why: Here 'correction' can be misread as 'a correction applied to the simulation'. 'Validité' is clearer.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The two advantage criteria, the 2026 timeline, the qLDPC caveat and the roadmap dates all match the source, and core terms are used consistently (tolérance aux fautes, atténuation des erreurs, qubits logiques). A native editor would still fix several calques and stiff phrasings: "n'est pas attendue comme étant viable dans l'immédiat proche" [18], "guidée par un focus sur" [25], "nous avons appris la motivation pour utiliser" [4] and "les grandes vues d'ensemble" [28]. There are also small grammar slips: "le C-API" should be "l'API C" (feminine), and "Si IBM est engagé" should read "s'est engagé".

examples.source: the implementation of full fault-tolerance is not expected to be viable in the immediate near term
examples.translation: la mise en œuvre d'une tolérance aux fautes complète n'est pas attendue comme étant viable dans l'immédiat proche
examples.suggested: la mise en œuvre d'une tolérance aux fautes complète ne devrait pas être viable à court terme
examples.why: This copies the English passive structure word for word, and "l'immédiat proche" is not idiomatic French.

examples.source: is driven by a focus on increasing qubit scale and connectivity
examples.translation: est guidée par un focus sur l'augmentation de l'échelle et de la connectivité des qubits
examples.suggested: est axée sur l'augmentation du nombre et de la connectivité des qubits
examples.why: "un focus sur" is an anglicism, and "guidée par un focus" is a calque of the English.

examples.source: we have learned about the motivation for using both high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing
examples.translation: nous avons appris la motivation pour utiliser à la fois le calcul haute performance (HPC) et le calcul quantique
examples.suggested: nous avons vu pourquoi il est intéressant d'utiliser à la fois le calcul haute performance (HPC) et le calcul quantique
examples.why: "apprendre la motivation pour" is a calque and not idiomatic French.

examples.source: the C-API (2025)
examples.translation: le C-API (2025)
examples.suggested: l'API C (2025)
examples.why: API is feminine in French, and the usual form is "l'API C".

examples.source: We have explored the big pictures and big ideas ... While IBM is committed to delivering
examples.translation: Nous avons exploré les grandes vues d'ensemble et les grandes idées ... Si IBM est engagé à fournir
examples.suggested: Nous avons exploré la vue d'ensemble et les grandes idées ... Si IBM s'est engagé à fournir
examples.why: "les grandes vues d'ensemble" is redundant and awkward, and "être engagé à" should be "s'être engagé à".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing here would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still fix a few things. Entanglement is "intrication/intriquer" everywhere except [29], which switches to "enchevêtré", a non-standard term in French quantum computing. The VQE gloss in [5], "solveur propre quantique variationnel", is a garbled calque of "eigensolver". "Expectation value" is rendered throughout as the calque "valeur attendue" where "valeur moyenne" or "espérance" is the usual term. [31] drops "match to the target state", and [28] has calques ("aussi faible que raisonnable", "sera revisité").

examples.source: the last qubit is not entangled with the others at all
examples.translation: le dernier qubit n'est pas du tout enchevêtré avec les autres
examples.suggested: le dernier qubit n'est pas du tout intriqué avec les autres (and « soit être intriqué avec les autres »)
examples.why: The rest of the file uses the standard term intrication/intriquer. Enchevêtré is non-standard in French QI and breaks consistency.

examples.source: a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE)
examples.translation: un solveur propre quantique variationnel (VQE)
examples.suggested: un solveur quantique variationnel de valeurs propres (VQE)
examples.why: « Solveur propre » is a meaningless literal split of 'eigensolver'. The eigenvalue sense is lost.

examples.source: determine the expectation value of the Hamiltonian
examples.translation: déterminer la valeur attendue de l'Hamiltonien
examples.suggested: déterminer la valeur moyenne (l'espérance) du hamiltonien
examples.why: « Valeur attendue » is a calque. French physics texts use « valeur moyenne » or « espérance ». It is recognizable, so this is minor.

examples.source: is not likely to yield a substantially better match to the target state than two or three repetitions
examples.translation: ne donnera vraisemblablement pas un résultat sensiblement meilleur que deux ou trois répétitions
examples.suggested: ne permettra vraisemblablement pas de s'approcher sensiblement mieux de l'état cible qu'avec deux ou trois répétitions
examples.why: This drops the reference to the target state, which is the point of comparison. Meaning is only slightly flattened.

examples.source: keep the circuit depth as low as is reasonable ... will be revisited in later sections
examples.translation: maintenir la profondeur du circuit aussi faible que raisonnable ... sera revisité dans les sections ultérieures
examples.suggested: garder une profondeur de circuit aussi faible que possible dans la limite du raisonnable ... sera abordé à nouveau dans les sections suivantes
examples.why: Calqued English phrasing that a native technical writer would rephrase.

editor_note: The technical content is accurate throughout: the Jordan-Wigner derivation, the |0>/|1> occupation-convention note and the tetrahedral-lattice encoding all match the source. The one change in meaning is in the conclusion [87]. "This isn't something anyone can just pick up" became "pas quelque chose que tout le monde peut", which means "not everyone can" rather than "no one can", so the encouragement is weaker. The other issues are about naturalness. "Mapping" is rendered both as "correspondance" and as the anglicism "mapper/mappera" ([55], [79], [80]). There are calques and stiff phrasing: "À un niveau élevé", "Passons à travers un exemple", the archaic "fussent", "encodages de Bravyi-Kitaev et d'encodage par parité", "ferromagnet" and "non-interactives". There is also one "notez" that breaks the tu register.

editor_note: In [86], "transpile" is rendered as "on transpose le circuit". Transposing a matrix or unitary is a different operation, so a learner could think the circuit is transposed 20 times, even though [85] correctly says "transpiler". In [70], the sentence "Thus we must optimize our circuit for each data point pair" is missing. That sentence explains why steps 2 and 3 are merged, so without it "Ainsi" no longer follows from the sentence before. There are also smaller slips: gender errors in [7] ("un fort intrication", "insuffisant"), "au l'état" in [16], and inconsistent terms. [29] switches to "matrice de noyau", "nous" and the English "feature map" where the rest of the file uses "matrice noyau", "on" and "plongement de caractéristiques". [58] uses "atténuation d'erreurs" where the rest of the file uses "mitigation d'erreurs".

examples.suggested: Ici, on transpile le circuit de chevauchement unitaire 20 fois
examples.why: 'Transposer' names the matrix transpose operation, which is a real and different concept for unitaries. It contradicts 'transpiler' in [85] and would mislead a learner about what is done.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner, but a native editor would change some terminology. The heading "Déflexion Quantique Variationnelle" [71] uses the word for "deflection". The eigenvalue technique is "déflation", so the heading misnames the core idea of VQD. "Observable" switches gender: feminine in [27] and [42] ("l'observable suivante", "une observable"), masculine in [72], [78], [98] and [110] ("un observable", "le nouvel observable"). Linear systems are called "consistant" [127, 129], an anglicism; French says "compatible". "Bootstrap" is rendered as both "Amorcer" [21, 64] and "Initialiser" [96, 140], and "Theoretical layout" as both "Organisation théorique" and "Structure théorique". One more point: in [108] the French says "n'a pas été intégrée" where the English literally says transpilation "has been built in". The next sentence of the source shows the negation is what was meant, so the French is right, but the source probably has a typo worth checking upstream.

examples.suggested: Déflation quantique variationnelle (VQD)

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The shock condition (t < -1/a when a < 0), the 13 vs 3021/4701 parameter comparison, the 0.0015 loss after 28 iterations and the RANDOM initialization caveat all match the source, and the terms stay consistent (tirs, qubits, EDP, non visqueuse, backend). There are a few calques a native editor would fix. "décrits de manière ubiquitaire" in [9] copies "ubiquitously". "résistance au mouvement ou à la déformation dépendante du taux" in [30] leaves it unclear what depends on the rate. "approche basée sur le quantique" in [45] is stiff.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The numbers (56 qubits, na*nt*nq, 30-day steps, (num_generations + 1) * population_size) and the caveat about the disabled multiple_passmanager all match the source. The title in [1] doesn't match its English: it reads "Optimiseur de Portefeuille Quantique - Une Fonction Qiskit par Global Data Quantum" where the source is "Dynamic portfolio optimization with Global Data Quantum's Portfolio Optimizer", which suggests a stale title. In [32], "primitive settings" became "paramètres primitifs" when it should be the settings of the primitives. Several calques remain: "Optimisation Binaire Non Contrainte Quadratique" with odd word order, "efficace en matériel" for "hardware-efficient", "Cela résulte en un problème", "nous exécutons l'optimisation en exécutant", and the redundant "mesures clés associées à la solution associée". Names also use English-style title case ("Optimiseur de Portefeuille Quantique", "Évolution Différentielle").

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The QPE mechanics, the noise caveat in [8], φ=1/6 in [19] and the Fire Opal claim in [31] all match the source. There are three minor slips. Entry [4] switches to the formal "Votre temps d'exécution" on a page that otherwise uses "tu". Entry [8] calques "binary expansion" twice as "expansion binaire", where standard French mathematics says "développement binaire". Entry [11] renders "visualization support" as "le support de visualisation", which is an anglicism; "la prise en charge de la visualisation" is the usual phrasing.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The T1/T2, SPAM and RB explanations, and the caveat in [51] that gains shrink as the chain gets longer, all keep their meaning. The main problem is mixed register. The first half addresses the reader as vous ("Vous apprendrez" [6], "sélectionnez"/"obtenez" [20]/[21], "Vous pouvez constater" [37]), while [9], [45], [51] and [53] correctly use tu. Two smaller points: [42] turns "requested backend properties" into "propriétés rapportées du backend demandé", which moves the qualifier onto a different word. [51] also has a stiff calque, "devient moins substantielle".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The caveats in [17] and [44] (only bit-flips are corrected, and only classical information is protected) and the list of error states in [15] match the English. The polish problems are these. "Bit-flip" is rendered three ways: "code de retournement de bit (bit-flip code)", "code bit-flip" and "erreurs bit-flip" / "les bit-flips". "Rounds" is left in English in [29]. [14] uses the calque "avec le support du groupe de Pauli", which reads as "with the help of" rather than the mathematical support. The step headings are also inconsistent: "Étape 1." and "Étape 3." use a period while "Étape 2 :" and "Étape 4 :" use a colon, and step 4 is a noun phrase while the others are verbs.

examples.source: Stabilizer codes critically focus on correcting a discrete error set with support from the Pauli group $\Pi^n$.
examples.translation: Les codes stabilisateurs se concentrent de manière cruciale sur la correction d'un ensemble discret d'erreurs avec le support du groupe de Pauli $\Pi^n$.
examples.suggested: Les codes stabilisateurs visent avant tout à corriger un ensemble discret d'erreurs dont le support est dans le groupe de Pauli $\Pi^n$.
examples.why: 'Avec le support' reads as 'with the help of' rather than the mathematical support, and 'de manière cruciale' is a stiff calque of 'critically'.

examples.why: 'Rounds' is left in English, while the rest of the file uses 'cycles' for the same idea ([15], [31]).

examples.source: The bit-flip code is among the simplest examples of a stabilizer code.
examples.translation: Le code de retournement de bit est l'un des exemples les plus simples de code stabilisateur.

examples.why: The same concept alternates with 'code bit-flip' ([15], [29]) and 'erreurs bit-flip' / 'les bit-flips' ([17], [44]).

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the precision of 0.05, the three jobs, t/2 circuit layers, the QPU-minute estimates and the private-job caveat, so nothing would mislead a learner. Several calques need a native editor's touch. "unique layer" became "couche unique", which French readers take as "single layer" rather than "distinct layer". [0] reads "mitigation d'erreurs de post-traitement logiciel" where "par post-traitement" is meant. Other stiff renderings are "est zéro" (should be "est nul"), "Passer à l'échelle TEM pour de grands circuits", "à l'échelle utilitaire", "apprentisseur de bruit" and "ID de job imprimé" (should be "affiché").

examples.why: 'couche unique' reads as 'single layer' in French. 'Distincte' keeps the meaning of 'unique'. The 'ainsi que la caractérisation' clause also breaks the parallel structure.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Quantities (20 vs 200 trials, max_iterations 4 vs 8, 15 and 100 qubits), caveats (fidelity tracks depth only statistically, StarPreRouting only helps on star sub-circuits) and comparisons all survive, and terminology is consistent (placement, routage, passe, gestionnaire de passes, profondeur 2Q). The problems are all in the French itself. There are grammar slips: "notre personnalisé" has no noun [42], and "la graine a presque aucun effet" is missing "n'" [70]. Some phrasing is calqued, such as "les avantages des deux augmentations d'essais" [45], "résultant dans le circuit SABRE uniquement le plus profond" [54] and "substantiellement en avance sur même la meilleure" [72]. The survey line mixes "Veuillez" with "tes" [77].

examples.suggested: le `SabreLayout` interne est désormais notre version personnalisée
